To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) at nonresonance the Galerkin discretizations of the Electric Field integral equation converge quasi-optimally; (b) at resonance the Galerkin method is well-posed and converges quasi-optimally in a suitable norm; (c) at resonance the spurious currents radiate only very weakly in the domain exterior to the scatterer; (d) the Galerkin approximation of the Electric Field Equation is well-posed in the resonant case
the Galerkin discretizations of the Electric Field integral Equation are stable and converge quasi-optimally in a wide range of frequencies, including resonant frequencies.

(1) the electric field integral operator has discrete Fredholm properties in the sense that the range of its adjoint is closed, (2) the Galerkin discretized EFIE has quasi-optimal convergence at non-resonant frequencies, and (3) the Galerki discretized EFIE is well-posed at resonant frequencies, provided that the spurious currents in the domain are not excited
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of Galerkin discretizations of the electric field integral equations in the presence of a resonant frequency.

the analysis of the Electric Field integral equation in the framework of the theory of discrete compact and Fredholm operators, with applications to the numerical approximation of the electric field integral operator.
the convergence of the Galerkirn discretization of the E.F.I.E. in the resonant case and the derivation of quasi-optimal convergence rates at non-resonant frequencies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Galerkin method is a robust numerical method for solving the EFIE at nonresonances, and that it is a stable numerical method for solving it at resonances.
the Galerkin discretized EFIE is well posed for any frequency.
the Electric Field Integral equation is well suited for the numerical treatment of the scattering problem, both at nonresonance and resonance frequencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Galerkin discretizations are stable for all frequencies, and that the convergence rate is quasi-optimal for nonresonant problems.
we show how the Galerkin discretized EFIE can be made into an accurate and robust method for solving electromagnetic scattering problems.
we have developed the theory of Galerkin discretizations of integral equations to a level where it is applicable in practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Electric Field Integral equation can be discretized with the Galerkin method without the need of a stabilization technique.
the electric currents in the exterior are small, even when the Galerkin approximation of the electric field is not.
the Galerkin discretizations of the EFIE are well-conditioned, provided that the resonant frequencies are not too close to one another.
